sentences.text:
THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 26.2.2014 PASSED IN MVC NO.764/2013 ON THE FILE OF THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE,
JMFC, SAKALESHPUR, PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR  ORAL JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for short) challenging the judgment and award dated 26.02.2014 passed in MVC No.764/2013, on the file of the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Sakaleshpur, seeking enhancement of the compensation.
The factum of accident and injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident are not in dispute.

3. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the material on records.
4.
The Tribunal has granted the compensation under various heads as follows:

Sl . Particulars Amount  No. (in.Rs.)
 1. Pain and agony 15,000.00  2. Injuries 3, 3000x3 9,000.00 Mohan vs Vidyashankar on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134320548/
2
3 . Loss of enjoyment 40,000.00

4. Attendant charges, special diet, 3,000.00  etc.
 5. Medical expenses 23,158.00  Total 90,158.00  5.
The Tribunal while determining the compensation has not adopted the correct parameters.
Hence, the claimant is entitled for enhanced compensation.

In the present case, as per the wound certificate-Ex.P7, it is proved that the claimant has sustained following injuries:
 i) Red short right eye  ii) Swelling and tenderness over the right  zygomatice region.
 iii) Restricted mouth opening  iv) Fracture of zygomatic maxilla  v) Tenderness over the right clavicular.
7. Considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant, the compensation amount awarded under the head 'pain and agony' is on the lower side.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.30,000/- is enhanced under the said head.
The compensation awarded under the head 'medical expenses' is as per the medical bills produced by the claimant and therefore, the same is kept in tact.

8. The Tribunal has not granted compensation under the head 'loss of income due to disability' on the reason that the claimant has suffered injury on the face, which is not affecting the work of 'Plumber'.
The claimant is a 'Plumber' by profession.

Though the claimant has NC:
2024:KHC:51080 suffered the above stated injuries, certainly it affects the work of 'Plumber'.
As the work of 'Plumber' is sensitive, it requires physical strength.

Therefore, though the doctor has stated that the claimant has suffered 20% of physical impairment and esthetic disability towards face and mouth and it does not affect the work of 'Plumber', the work of 'Plumber' requires physical strength.

When mouth is restricted, the right eye is affected and fracture of zygomatic maxilla certainly affects the work of 'Plumber', therefore, 7% as permanent partial disability towards whole body is taken into consideration.
The accident is caused in the year 2012.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.7,000/- is to be taken into consideration as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

As the Mohan vs Vidyashankar on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134320548/
3 claimant was aged 31 years, the appropriate multiplier applicable is '15'.

sentences.text:
Hence, the 'loss of future earnings due to disability' is hereby reassessed the quantified as under:
Rs.7000 x 7/100 x 15 x 12 = Rs.88,200/-
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.88,200/- is awarded under the head 'loss of future earnings due to disability'.

The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.3,000/- under the head 'attendant charges'
which is on the lesser side.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.15,000/- is enhanced under the said head.
Further, the Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head 'loss of amenities' which is on the higher side.
The same is reduced to Rs.25,000/-. under the said head.
10. The Tribunal has not awarded the compensation under the head 'loss of earnings during laid up period'.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.14,000/- (7000 x 2 months) is awarded under the said head.

11. Thus, in all, the claimant is entitled for the following sums:
Sl.

No . Particulars Compensation awarded (in Rs.)
1. Pain and suffering 30,000.00 2. Loss of future earning 88,200.00 capacity due to disability 3.
Medical expenses 23,158.00 NC: 2024:KHC:51080 4.
Incidental expenses like 15,000.00 conveyance, special diet & Attendant charges 5. Loss of earnings during laid 14,000.00 up period 6. Loss of amenities 25,000.00 TOTAL 1,95,358.00 12.
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation of Rs.90,158/-, but the appellant/claimant is entitled to total compensation of Rs.1,95,358/-.

Therefore, the appellant/claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation of Rs.1,05,200/- (Rs.1,95,358 - Rs.90,158) with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.

13. Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.764/2013 dated 26.02.2014 by the Court of the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Sakaleshpur is hereby modified holding that the claimant is entitled Mohan vs Vidyashankar on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134320548/
4 for enhanced compensation of Rs.1,05,200/- along NC: 2024:KHC:51080 with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization, in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. The appellant-claimant is not entitled for the interest for the delayed period of 145 days in filing the appeal.

iv. Costs made easy.
v. Ordered accordingly.
vi.
The other observations and findings of the Tribunal  are kept in tact.

SD/-
 (HANCHATE SANJEEVKUMAR)
 JUDGE KA CT:
